summary: P3 examples — make the worked examples REAL gate-clean (today the surfaced example is the P0 stub; this fills the real multi-language examples so the cold-start front-load shows a genuine gate-passing one). P3.1 move EXAMPLE_TEMPLATES from MissionBriefingSupport.ts (around lines 106-213, single consumer MissionBriefingBuilder.ts:46) DOWN into the module recipe-authoring-spec/examples/; MissionBriefingSupport.ts re-imports them downward (workflows imports domain is legal). Per section C.9 the down-move is INTERNAL-only: MissionBriefingSupport must NOT re-export EXAMPLE_TEMPLATES (host-agent/index.ts:75 export-star would leak a domain symbol through the stable-public @alembic/core/host-agent-workflows facade) — consumers needing examples import example(lang) from @alembic/core/knowledge; re-run npm run check boundary and intentionally update the snapshot; grep-prove the EXAMPLE_TEMPLATES constant body does not depend on a workflows-layer import. CRITICAL FIX (section C.5): all four shipped examples FAIL the gate today — CONTENT_CONTRAST_MISSING (a marker line like // ✅ 正确 leaves only 2 trimmed chars after the marker, below the 4-char floor) and objectivec also fails DO_CLAUSE_NON_IMPERATIVE (Prefix is not in the allowlist). Rewrite every shipped example so it PASSES the full gate: each ✅ and ❌ marker line carries >=4 non-space chars after the marker (e.g. // ✅ correct: @interface BDVideoPlayer), and every doClause leads with an allowlisted imperative verb. P3.2 add the missing real languages (swift, kotlin, java, go, rust, csharp, javascript, and any other primary corpus languages) so unlisted languages no longer fall to the skeletal _default, and grow _default to gate-passing. P3.3 injection: Core MissionBriefingBuilder keeps its injection; the Plugin cold-start (P2.3) and the AlembicAgent bootstrap producer (P1.4b) already surface example() — note that; the in-process main-body ColdStartWorkflow/KnowledgeRescanWorkflow injection is a carry-item (ai-scan is carved out; if the bootstrap in-process path already renders example via the upgraded producer, grep-prove it, else record as follow-up). THE STANDING TRIPWIRE (section C.5): add test/recipe-authoring-spec/examples-gate-passing.test.ts that runs EVERY example(lang) through validateAgainst(candidate, {stage:'all'}) and asserts zero violations — this guarantees the shipped examples are gate-passing forever, the opposite of today's anti-examples. Acceptance on node 22: Core build:check green; the examples-gate-passing test green (every example, all languages incl _default, passes the full gate); the EXAMPLE_TEMPLATES move did not break MissionBriefingBuilder injection (briefing tests green); npm run check boundary green with the intentionally-updated snapshot (no facade leak); full Core test green. The 3 pre-existing lint:naming files are the out-of-scope carve-out. Discipline: the examples must genuinely PASS validateAgainst (do NOT relax the gate to make a bad example pass — fix the example); the down-move stays internal (no facade leak); main only, no push or tag or version bump; FieldSpec unchanged; do not touch the gates (byte-identical from P1) or the dead duplicates; ai-scan carved out. Producer-consumer: this fills example() so the already-wired cold-start front-load surfaces a real gate-clean example; P4 (drift + parity suite) and P5 (real-machine) follow. Backfill the Core commit, the examples-gate-passing proof (every example passes the full gate), the anti-example fixes (before/after marker lines + the objectivec verb fix), the languages added, the boundary snapshot update, and raw build and test output.
sourceRef: Design/docs/current/alembic-recipe-authoring-guidance-optimization-2026-06-29.md sections B-P3 (P3.1/P3.2/P3.3), C.5 (anti-examples fail the gate + self-consistency tripwire), C.9 (down-move internal-only) plus the shipped module examples folder (P0 stub) + validateAgainst in @alembic/core/knowledge
